purpose: Prepare macOS-specific synthetic fixtures and a static distribution-check matrix before implementing native platform behavior or producing signed artifacts.

dependencyGateDetails.rule: Until both dependencies are accepted, only synthetic fixture/interface planning is allowed. Do not implement platform behavior, build/sign/notarize/package, install or update an app, run real-device behavior, or use user data.

sections: §5 所有页面必须覆盖的状态

macosSpecificSemantics: capture target/application identity through public macOS capabilities
permission denial retains copy/search capability where available
menu-bar, multi-display, signing, notarization, and macOS update behavior require macOS evidence
windowsSemanticsNotAssumed: UIPI error diagnosis or AllowSetForegroundWindow authorization
platformBoundary.sharedBoundary: Only accepted platform-neutral contracts and user-visible safety outcomes may be shared. Windows helper APIs and helper deadlines are not automatically macOS requirements; native macOS deadlines and API behavior need macOS-specific evidence. This plan does not claim that a Windows fixture, mock, or API result proves macOS behavior.

fixturePolicy.futureDeviceScope: Any later native acceptance uses a disposable macOS test account/device, synthetic pasteboard content, a dedicated receiver, and a test-only shortcut. Native changeCount, target/application identity, Accessibility allow/denied copy-only behavior, two-display placement, menu-bar/startup/hotkey operation, cancellation, cache, and UI responsiveness require macOS-hosted evidence before their gates can close; Windows evidence cannot close them. Login-item and permission-state fixtures use a disposable account provisioned before the run and never mutate the user account. Release acceptance uses candidate-matched signed/notarized artifacts and synthetic local data in that disposable environment.
neverUse: live user profile, clipboard, account, or application data
developer signing private keys, notarization credentials, or personal Apple account credentials in repository files or reports
Windows behavior as a substitute for a macOS result
build, sign, notarize, install, or update an app during this fixture-only task
fixturePolicy.resultAssertions: Prefer observable synthetic content, changeCount, target identity stability, permission capability state, copy/paste side-effect counts, process/UI state, and artifact metadata. Do not invent exact error/result mappings or user authorization copy.
fixturePolicy.evidencePrivacy: Later evidence may contain OS/build/architecture, sanitized signing identity reference, artifact hashes, permission state, timings, and synthetic IDs/counts. Never include clipboard payloads, signing secrets, tokens, or user content.
fixturePolicy.statusMeaning: NOT_RUN means the behavior or release check has not been executed. This plan is not an implementation, build, signing result, notarization result, or platform-support claim.
fixturePolicy.futureReleaseScope: Only after T11/T12 are accepted and release identity, notarization criteria, updater protocol, and schema compatibility are approved may a disposable macOS test account exercise a candidate-matched update/rollback pair. No production channel, user data, personal Apple account credentials, or signing secrets are used.

fixtureCases.input: A fake macOS pasteboard adapter has already captured a deterministic synthetic image. It returns one changeCount and delivers several duplicate notifications for that value without changing image bytes.
fixtureCases.action: Feed duplicate notifications through the synthetic capture adapter and observe enqueue/coalescing and encoder calls.
fixtureCases.expected: Do not assert a duplicate-notification coalescing or capture-count policy until it is frozen. Re-encoding the unchanged clipboard image must remain zero per limits.v1.json performanceTargets.sameClipboardImageReencodes; that assertion is independent of how many notifications are admitted.
fixtureCases.observation: Record changeCount, notification count, capture jobs, content digest/byte length, and encoder call count only; never record image pixels.

fixtureCases.input: Two successive synthetic pasteboard states have distinct changeCount values and distinct harmless markers.
fixtureCases.action: Deliver one notification for each count and read through the fake adapter.
fixtureCases.expected: Each new changeCount is treated as a new clipboard version. Result summaries identify the correct synthetic version and never substitute an older read result.
fixtureCases.observation: Record old/new counts, capture IDs, response order, and digest/byte length only.

fixtureCases.input: A synthetic read for count A is delayed; the fake pasteboard advances to count B before A completes.
fixtureCases.action: Deliver B's notification, complete B, then release delayed A.
fixtureCases.expected: The older A result cannot overwrite or re-enqueue as the current B version. Cancellation/retry outcome remains bounded and no user clipboard data is involved.
fixtureCases.observation: Record count/job ordering, visible synthetic version, stale-read suppression, and adapter call counts.

fixtureCases.input: A synthetic pasteboard representation is temporarily unavailable to a fake read adapter, then becomes readable; a second case never becomes readable.
fixtureCases.action: Exercise bounded retry and a changed changeCount while retry is pending.
fixtureCases.expected: A newer changeCount cancels stale read work and retry remains bounded. Do not reuse Windows helper deadlines for a native macOS pasteboard read; macOS retry count/deadline and terminal error mapping remain OPEN_QUESTION. Unbounded retry is not acceptable.
fixtureCases.observation: Record attempt count, elapsed time, count observed per attempt, cancellation state, and final capability category only.

fixtureCases.input: A synthetic host adapter reports a target application identity and a separate ClipNest-owned/self target identity.
fixtureCases.action: Capture target identity before panel presentation, then request the self target as a negative case.
fixtureCases.expected: The application uses the public macOS target/application capability and excludes its own panel as an external target. Windows HWND/PID identity fields are not assumed.
fixtureCases.observation: Record opaque synthetic identity IDs, validity/self classification, and capability calls; exact native identity fields remain OPEN_QUESTION.

fixtureCases.input: The fake target identity changes or becomes unavailable after capture but before the final paste check.
fixtureCases.action: Continue the synthetic action after invalidation.
fixtureCases.expected: No input is sent to a stale/replaced target; a completed supported clipboard copy remains available as copy-only. Exact terminal error code is not assumed.
fixtureCases.observation: Record captured/current synthetic identity, clipboard state class, input count, and visible fallback category.

fixtureCases.input: A dedicated synthetic target app is minimized using a fake platform state; a separate scenario has the user switch to another app during restoration.
fixtureCases.action: Request one synthetic paste and observe any target restoration/focus transitions.
fixtureCases.expected: Only the originally captured target may be considered; if it cannot be verified or user intent changes, automatic input stops and copy-only remains. The specific macOS restoration API and policy are OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record synthetic target identity timeline, restoration calls, frontmost app class, and input count.

fixtureCases.input: Synthetic monitor topology metadata for a two-display Mac setup, including safe-area/work-area and scale values supplied by the fake adapter.
fixtureCases.action: Open/hide the synthetic panel from a target associated with each display and inspect bounds and operability.
fixtureCases.expected: The panel remains visible and operable without clipping on the selected display. Display-selection rule, mixed scale, notch/menu-bar safe area, virtual/RDP displays, and hot-plug coverage remain OPEN_QUESTION; no Windows coordinate rule is reused.
fixtureCases.observation: Record display IDs, safe-area/scale metadata, panel bounds, clipping, and selected-policy decision once frozen.

fixtureCases.input: Synthetic app host is initialized with the panel hidden and a running fake core/repository worker.
fixtureCases.action: Use the macOS menu-bar/status-item entry to show and hide the panel while a synthetic repository operation is active.
fixtureCases.expected: The menu-bar entry provides the specified panel lifecycle and hiding the panel does not stop the background core operation. macOS menu-item labels and exact activation/click semantics remain OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record activation source, panel state, process/worker state, generation IDs, and summary-only events.

fixtureCases.input: Fake macOS startup capability is separately configured as enabled, disabled, and unavailable by the synthetic settings adapter.
fixtureCases.action: Inspect the settings state and simulated next-launch behavior without registering a real login item.
fixtureCases.expected: The UI reflects the supplied capability and does not claim startup is enabled when registration is unavailable. Whether/how the OS prompts, requires explicit user activation, or reports a pending state is OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record capability state, visible setting, fake registration call count, and simulated launch outcome.

fixtureCases.input: A synthetic shortcut registration collides with a fake existing owner; no real system shortcut is registered.
fixtureCases.action: Attempt registration, then invoke the panel through a declared alternative synthetic activation path.
fixtureCases.expected: The app does not claim the global shortcut is active and does not steal/loop on the conflict. Search/copy remains available through supported UI. Exact conflict reason mapping and user-facing recovery wording are OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record fake registration result, capability value, visible notice category, and copy/search callback counts.

fixtureCases.input: A disposable macOS test account/device has an explicitly authorized synthetic test app and a dedicated receiver with a fixed harmless marker.
fixtureCases.action: Run the supported automatic-input flow once and independently inspect receiver content.
fixtureCases.expected: Only after the host reports the required capability as available and the captured target still matches may the synthetic receiver observe the marker once. A host/IPC acknowledgement alone is not target-observation evidence.
fixtureCases.observation: Record macOS/build/architecture, synthetic target observation, capability category, and call count; do not alter the user's Accessibility setting.

fixtureCases.input: The synthetic capability adapter reports Accessibility authorization denied while pasteboard copy/search are available.
fixtureCases.action: Search/select synthetic content, copy it, and attempt the automatic-input action once.
fixtureCases.expected: Copy and search remain usable; no automatic input is claimed or sent; the UI offers an authorization/settings route. Exact system prompt/settings wording is OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record capability snapshot, search/copy outcomes, input count, and visible notice category without changing OS permission state.

fixtureCases.input: The adapter reports unknown, temporarily unavailable, or unsupported Accessibility capability in distinct synthetic cases.
fixtureCases.action: Render each state and invoke only the explicitly available copy/search controls.
fixtureCases.expected: Unknown/unavailable permission is never treated as authorized; no automatic input occurs. The app presents a truthful capability state and preserves copy/search when supported. Whether to request permission automatically or only after user action remains OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record synthetic status class, visible action availability, prompt/request call count, and input count.

fixtureCases.input: A fake paste job is paused before input commit; capability changes from authorized to denied/unknown.
fixtureCases.action: Resume the job after the capability change and separately cancel it during a blocked focus step.
fixtureCases.expected: The job does not continue to input on stale permission/target state; cancellation control remains responsive. Already-issued asynchronous OS calls may not be reversible; no later action is scheduled after cancellation.
fixtureCases.observation: Record capability transition, cancellation latency, subsequent platform calls, and input count.

fixtureCases.input: Synthetic text and image content with an invalid target or unavailable autoPaste capability, while pasteboard writing remains supported.
fixtureCases.action: Invoke explicit copy and one automatic-input attempt.
fixtureCases.expected: Clipboard copy remains available; automatic input is reported as unavailable/copied-only and is not retried. Exact user-facing wording and native result discriminant remain OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record pasteboard change category, capability snapshot, panel state, copy/input counts, and visible result category.

fixtureCases.input: A synthetic paste job is held before its pasteboard write commit point.
fixtureCases.action: Cancel and release the preparation barrier.
fixtureCases.expected: Accepted cancellation before commit produces no pasteboard write or input submission; no delayed callback later performs either side effect.
fixtureCases.observation: Record cancellation state/timing and pasteboard/input call counts.

fixtureCases.input: A fake macOS focus/permission operation is held while its control path remains available. A future controlled Mac host uses a synthetic adapter barrier and disposable receiver; no user app is targeted.
fixtureCases.action: Cancel the job, release the blocked adapter call, and inspect native host control responsiveness separately from any already-issued OS call.
fixtureCases.expected: Cancellation ordering prevents any not-yet-issued restoration or input after acceptance. Do not assume the Windows helper ACK deadline applies to macOS. Native cancellation deadline, already-issued native-call interruption, and supervision mapping remain OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record cancel latency, host availability, operation release order, and post-cancel calls; native timing is not accepted against a Windows helper deadline.

fixtureCases.input: A fake job reaches its single input commit point, then its acknowledgement is lost; cancellation/reopen follows.
fixtureCases.action: Inspect the terminal state and replay the same user intent once through the fixture adapter.
fixtureCases.expected: The system does not claim cancellation rolled back a committed action and does not automatically duplicate an action with an unknown result. Exact macOS-specific terminal enum remains OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record commit ordering, request/job identity, replay count, and side-effect count.

fixtureCases.input: Synthetic unique and duplicate changeCount notifications arrive while one capture worker is blocked; queue pressure is driven around the configured captureQueueItems limit.
fixtureCases.action: Release the worker, change the active count, and inspect queued jobs and cancellation behavior.
fixtureCases.expected: Configured queue and worker limits are not exceeded; duplicate/current-sequence work may be coalesced only as specified, and any overflow is visible rather than silently promising every transient clipboard change was retained. Exact overflow result mapping is OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record queue depth, unique counts, worker concurrency, overflow counter, current generation, and accepted/rejected synthetic IDs.

fixtureCases.input: A deterministic synthetic image is tested as unchanged cache hit and as cache miss with a controllable decode barrier.
fixtureCases.action: Deliver duplicate changeCount notifications for the hit case; select the miss case while interacting with search/cancel controls.
fixtureCases.expected: Unchanged image re-encoding is zero per limits.performanceTargets.sameClipboardImageReencodes. Cache-miss decoding remains off the UI/control path and configured worker/cache-count limits are observed. Numeric imageWorkerPeakBytes acceptance remains OPEN_QUESTION until T09 freezes allocation categories and measurement method.
fixtureCases.observation: Record changeCount, cache hit/miss, encode/decode counts, worker concurrency, raw peak observation only if available, UI/control responsiveness signal, and cancel progress; never save pixels. Raw peak is not a PASS metric.

fixtureCases.input: A synthetic repository operation/event is pending while the panel is hidden or WebView is recreated; no live profile is attached.
fixtureCases.action: Hide/reopen the menu-bar panel and deliver delayed prior-generation events after the new generation starts.
fixtureCases.expected: Background core work remains independent of panel visibility; stale events do not overwrite current UI state or trigger another paste. Database crash durability is not claimed by this fixture.
fixtureCases.observation: Record host/core process state, generations, summary/event IDs, and side-effect counts only.

fixtureCases.input: An isolated test host owns a synthetic idle worker and a separate cancellable pre-commit task.
fixtureCases.action: Exercise the declared menu-bar quit action and observe task cancellation and child cleanup.
fixtureCases.expected: After explicit quit, no delayed pasteboard/input action occurs and owned test children exit. Whether close hides to menu bar or quits is OPEN_QUESTION until a product rule is frozen.
fixtureCases.observation: Record process identities/exit states, cancellation class, and post-shutdown calls.

fixtureCases.input: Synthetic capability snapshots cover ready, permission_required, unsupported, and temporarily_unavailable states on the macOS adapter.
fixtureCases.action: Render capability-driven UI and select a supported copy/search operation for each state.
fixtureCases.expected: UI follows reported capability rather than OS-name assumptions. A Windows mock/status or T11 pass cannot set macOS autoPaste, target, pasteboard, or display capability to ready.
fixtureCases.observation: Record adapter/platform identity, capability fields/status, enabled actions, and copy/input callback counts.

fixtureCases.input: A future signed candidate's sanitized build manifest, entitlement inventory, bundle/architecture metadata, and CI secret-reference inventory; no artifact is created in this task.
fixtureCases.action: Review manifest-to-bundle identity consistency, declared entitlements against the accepted capability plan, signing identity reference, and repository/report secret hygiene.
fixtureCases.expected: The later review can trace which identity/entitlements signed the intended build and find no private signing credential in source or evidence. Team ID, bundle ID, minimum OS, architecture set, and entitlement allowlist are OPEN_QUESTION until release identity is approved.
fixtureCases.observation: Record sanitized artifact/build identifiers and boolean checks only; never include private keys or credential values.

fixtureCases.input: A future release evidence bundle containing build identity, notarization submission/result metadata, and artifact hash; no notarization is performed here.
fixtureCases.action: Verify that evidence refers to the same candidate artifact/build and that any required distribution status is explicitly recorded.
fixtureCases.expected: No macOS distribution/support claim is made without matching evidence for the actual candidate. Notarization channel, accepted status/ticket evidence, and exact rejection policy are OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record evidence references, artifact hash match, and result presence/status without credentials or user content.

fixtureCases.input: A future signed update manifest and candidate artifact metadata with synthetic previous/current version identifiers and hashes.
fixtureCases.action: Check version/architecture/artifact-hash references and the accepted signature-verification policy without downloading or installing an update.
fixtureCases.expected: A mismatched/unsigned metadata record is not treated as a valid update. Updater protocol, signing envelope, version-channel policy, and exact failure/error mapping are OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record synthetic versions, architectures, hash-match/signature-check booleans, and review result; no artifacts are executed.

fixtureCases.input: A future previous/current desktop version compatibility matrix and synthetic schema versions; no database or app is downgraded.
fixtureCases.action: Review whether a binary rollback can run without asking an older binary to write an unsupported newer schema; inspect the planned autoPaste-off rollback switch.
fixtureCases.expected: Rollback preserves local data and does not rely on automatic reverse migration. If compatibility is not proven, the plan keeps affected features disabled and records the user-visible limitation; exact compatibility window and feature switch mapping are OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record version/schema pairs, compatibility decision, feature-off indicator, and evidence links only.

fixtureCases.input: A future support matrix lists macOS versions, CPU architectures, and available controlled CI/device evidence.
fixtureCases.action: Compare each claimed supported row with a corresponding native capability/permission/signing/update evidence reference.
fixtureCases.expected: Unmeasured versions/architectures remain unsupported or explicitly unverified; no cross-platform result fills a macOS evidence gap. Minimum/current macOS versions, Intel/Apple Silicon support, and device availability are OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record matrix row count, evidence references, and rows marked unverified; do not claim support from this static plan.

fixtureCases.input: Only after T11/T12 are accepted and release identity, notarization criteria, updater protocol, and schema compatibility are approved: a signed/notarized baseline and candidate artifact pair with matching hashes/schema matrix is used on a disposable macOS test account with synthetic local data.
fixtureCases.action: On a supported controlled Mac device, verify candidate identity and matching signature/notarization references, then exercise the approved upgrade and compatible rollback path using the disposable synthetic profile.
fixtureCases.expected: Only the candidate matching the approved artifact identity/signature/notarization record is exercised. Upgrade, data preservation, and rollback behavior follow the approved version/schema matrix; incompatible rollback is blocked or affected autoPaste remains off as that matrix specifies. Exact updater/error policy remains OPEN_QUESTION.
fixtureCases.observation: Record macOS/build/architecture, sanitized artifact hashes/identity references, versions, synthetic schema/data verification class, and result only; no credentials or user content.

fixtureCases.input: A synthetic text canary and tiny synthetic image are processed by the isolated fixture, followed by a synthetic error path; test-only telemetry and crash serialization sinks are captured locally.
fixtureCases.action: Inspect serialized test output for exact canary values and prohibited raw content; do not submit or upload reports.
fixtureCases.expected: Clipboard body, title, source, image, key/token, and unsanitized SQL parameters never appear in telemetry/crash output; allowed diagnostic output contains sanitized status/IDs only.
fixtureCases.observation: Record canary-found booleans and output categories/counts only; do not place canary values or raw report bodies in evidence.

releaseStaticCheckMatrix.openQuestion: Team/bundle identity, architecture set, minimum OS, and entitlement allowlist are not frozen.
Notarization workflow/channel, evidence required for acceptance, and rejection handling are not frozen.
Updater protocol and exact signature/rollback failure mapping are not frozen.
Supported schema compatibility window and exact feature-off switch are not frozen.
Minimum/current supported macOS versions, CPU architectures, and test hardware/CI availability are not frozen.

openQuestions.reason: The task does not freeze a minimum macOS version, architecture support, or available signing/notarization test environment. Each claimed platform row will need its own native evidence.

The need for Accessibility authorization and copy/search fallback are specified, but the exact allowed/denied/unknown detection mapping, permission transition handling, status/result enum, and user-facing authorization text are not.

The implementation must use public macOS target/application capabilities, but exact identity lifetime/revalidation, minimized-app restoration, safe-area/menu-bar placement, and display-selection policy are not frozen. Windows HWND and monitor rules are not substitutes.

pasteboard.changeCount is the change signal and reads must be bounded, but duplicate notification coalescing, delayed-rendered retry count, overflow behavior, and exact terminal error mapping need a frozen contract.

The task calls for menu-bar/status-item, startup, and hotkey conflict coverage; precise activation/menu semantics, login-item opt-in/permission flow, conflict resolution, and user-facing copy are not specified.

The release plan requires macOS signing/notarization and upgrade/rollback compatibility, but identity/entitlements, notarization evidence rules, updater signature protocol, supported schema window, and release acceptance thresholds are not frozen.
No exact macOS permission/help copy or native failure reason strings are specified. Do not reuse Windows UIPI or focus-denial explanations.

The shared cancellation ordering/safety outcomes are reusable, but the Windows helper ACK deadline and worker-supervision implementation must not be assumed to govern macOS native API calls. Freeze the macOS host deadline, interruption limits for already-issued calls, and unavailable/recovery mapping before native cancellation acceptance.

T09 progress leaves imageWorkerPeakBytes allocation categories and measurement method unfrozen. T13 may observe a raw peak, but cannot assert numeric peak acceptance until that cross-task accounting contract is frozen.

requiredNotRunGates.reason: T13 depends on both T11 and T12; both are currently not_started, so native implementation, build, and platform behavior remain gated.
No macOS pasteboard, target identity, Accessibility, menu-bar, startup, shortcut, display, cancellation, queue, cache, or UI responsiveness operation has been performed.
No binary was built, signed, notarized, installed, updated, or rolled back. The release matrix above is planning only.
No native Mac device/CI platform was exercised and the support matrix is not frozen. Windows behavior is not used as evidence for macOS.

acceptanceReminder: Every native behavior and release-check case is NOT_RUN. Keep T13 not_started until T11/T12 are accepted, OPEN_QUESTION items are resolved as needed, macOS-version-specific controlled-device evidence exists for each claimed capability, signing/notarization/update/rollback evidence matches the candidate artifacts, and required review is complete.

acceptanceGateMatrix.futureFixture: Second disposable test process reserves only a test-only shortcut; never contend with user shortcuts
